subject: Math
prompt:
[Figure 1]

The scatterplot shows data set A, which consists of the heights $y$, in centimeters, of a tomato plant at various times, $x$, in weeks. The equation of a line of best fit for the relationship in data set A can be written as $y = -3.2 + 6.4x$, where $2 \le x \le 6$. The plant was measured again at $10$ weeks and had a height of $45$ centimeters. Data set B consists of all the data points in data set A as well as the data point $(10, 45)$. The equation of a line of best fit for data set B can be written as $y = r + sx$, where $r$ and $s$ are constants and $2 \le x \le 10$. Assuming the equations of the lines of best fit are calculated in the same way, which of the following is the best estimate for the value of $s$?
explanation: Choice C is correct. The equation of the line of best fit for data set A is $y = -3.2 + 6.4x$, which has a slope of $6.4$. Using this equation, the predicted height at $x = 10$ weeks would be $y = -3.2 + 6.4(10) = -3.2 + 64 = 60.8$ centimeters. However, the actual measured height at $10$ weeks was only $45$ centimeters, which is below the predicted value. When a data point falls below the line of best fit and is added to the data set, it pulls the line of best fit downward, resulting in a smaller slope. Therefore, the slope $s$ of the new line of best fit for data set B must be less than the original slope of $6.4$. Among the given choices, only $4.6$ is less than $6.4$, making it the best estimate for $s$.
